body:
# Independent audit: robust planar reweighting and rank-two sections

Audited `candidate 3ed6256a0896f434` and ran
`supporting computation verify_robust_planar_chord_reweighting.py` with the workspace math runtime.
Every exact symbolic identity and comparison passed. The following checks
address the geometric and measure dependencies not covered by that script.

## Selected-sector truncation

For strict noncollinear balanced chord triples, every balanced weight is
less than one half. Reweighting by q_i in [1,b] gives theta_i<=b/(1+b),
so every selected sector with value 1-theta_i has W>=1/(1+b). It is the
integral of W-c, rather than a bare average, that decreases under removal.

If a chord line through two marked boundary points is nonsupporting, those
points are the endpoints of its section of the convex body. For a point
on the removed side, its radial projection to the line lies both on the
segment from zero to that point and in the body. It therefore lies between
the marked endpoints. Hence the removed point belongs to exactly the
claimed angular sector. Supporting chord lines remove nothing.

The previously proved strict-hexagon construction applies independently of
the reweighting: its three selected cuts enclose T, and H=T intersect -T.
The complementary corners are in the sectors with values theta_i. The
linear-fractional corner-area relaxation has a positive denominator and
can indeed be minimized successively at box endpoints. No realization of
all box vertices by convex bodies is required.

## The finite multiplier patterns

For fixed t, the q-dependent part is a weighted mean of
a_i=t_i^2 1_(i in I), with positive base weights t_i(1-t_i). Its derivative
in q_i has the sign of a_i minus the current weighted mean. Therefore
a smallest-value coordinate can be set to b and a largest-value coordinate
to one at a minimum; any intermediate coordinate is set to either endpoint.
For two included corners this gives exactly (1,1,b),(b,1,b) after ordering.
For three corners it gives exactly (b,1,1),(b,b,1). Ties cause no omitted
case: a tied extremal coordinate may be assigned the indicated endpoint
without changing the objective. Zero-coordinate boundary cases are limits
or are checked directly by the displayed polynomials.

The one-corner estimate uses 24v<=6s^2 correctly. Both two-corner quadratic
certificates have the stated signs. The two all-corner expansions have
nonnegative coefficients. Their exact expansions, discriminant, and the
dimension comparisons were checked by the verifier.

## Degeneracy and projection measures

The modified gauge (1-e)p_L+e|.| gives a strictly convex body and scales
both p_i and -p_i by the same c_i. The transformed weights still balance.
Thus the strict-triple proof applies; Hausdorff convergence of convex bodies
gives L1 convergence of their area indicators. Closed cap lines have zero
planar area throughout.

For rank-two normals in a plane E, the section decomposition

    u_i perpendicular=(E intersect u_i perpendicular) direct-sum E perpendicular

is orthogonal. Its Euclidean measure is therefore the product measure with
Jacobian exactly one. This proves S_i=integral_line f and shows that the
projected first moment of a centered full section is the first moment of
the line density. The remaining section-centroid coordinates are not used.

Polar Fubini gives area(B intersect H)=integral_H f for the planar radial
body with rho_B(v)^2=2 integral t f(tv)dt, and likewise for total mass.
There is no missing normalization. Equal signed line first moments give
equal radial lengths in the two directions, hence a centered chord.

Finally r_i=S_i/[sqrt(f(0))L_i] and lambda_i proportional to theta_i r_i
give sum lambda_i L_i u_i=0. Writing chord vectors as
p_i=-(L_i/2)R(u_i) makes their oriented caps precisely the original caps.
Reweighting lambda_i by 1/r_i recovers theta_i. The centered-line comparison
therefore supplies exactly the advertised q ranges, with no extra Jacobian
or dimension factor.

Conclusion: the theorem is valid as stated for normal rank at most two.
It supplies no conclusion for rank-three or higher circuits and no mixed
fiber compatibility or OC conclusion by itself.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
